extracted.intended_audience: legal practitioners, policymakers, pension administrators, and claimants interested in QPP procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and evidentiary standards for initiating, examining, deciding, controlling, and seeking reconsideration of applications for Quebec Pension Plan (QPP) benefits (disability, retirement, survivor's, orphan's, death benefits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of decision (Board)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board must notify the applicant of the decision rendered immediately; notification must be in writing and must give reasons for the decision; the Board must inform the applicant of his right to apply for a reconsideration of the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule completes section 26; notification letters typically include reasons and advise on reconsideration rights and time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may present the application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application may be presented by a person other than the prospective beneficiary, provided that the former demonstrates his qualification to do so either by virtue of the Act or by proving his mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If presented by someone else, the applicant must show authority (statutory or mandatary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prescribed form (application)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be presented on the form prescribed for the purpose; a written declaration manifesting the applicant's intention to apply for benefits may, however, be accepted as equivalent to a notice of claim, provided that it is followed by an application according to the prescribed form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A simple written notice can start the one-year timeframe but should be followed by the prescribed form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing the application
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be addressed to an office of the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal requirement for proper routing and receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Onus of proof on applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The onus is on the applicant to produce in substantiation of his application the factual evidence establishing his right to benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must supply supporting documents; Board may request additional proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board's power to secure proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may, in order to secure proof of any fact, require a sworn statement or the production of pertinent documents, or undertake an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board can compel sworn statements, documents, or run investigations to verify claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of application within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: The application may be cancelled within 30 days of the date of issue of the first benefit cheque, provided that the cheque has not been cashed and without the decision rendered on the application prejudicing the determination of any subsequent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows applicants to withdraw shortly after initial payment if cheque uncashed; does not prejudice future applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility conditions for disability pension
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributor must be under 65 years of age and must have been contributing to the plan for at least five years; must be disabled (suffering from a severe and prolonged physical or mental disability, as recognized by the Board).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also see QPP sections 134–138, 155 (calculations) and sections 172–174, 181–185 (payment conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'severe and prolonged' disability
rubrics_metrics.description: A disability is severe only if by reason thereof the person is incapable regularly of pursuing any substantially gainful occupation; it is prolonged only if it is likely to result in death or to be of indefinite duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation follows federal caselaw: severity judged in light of both objective and subjective elements; Board recognizes non-medical factors (training, age, sex, occupational background).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'substantially gainful occupation'
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition is not limited to work in the applicant's usual field of employment, nor does the availability of employment in the region of the applicant's domicile affect capacity to 'regularly' pursue an occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment considers broader employment possibilities, not merely local job availability or prior occupation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child contributor's pension eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Child of a disabled contributor may apply if unmarried and under 18, or under 25 provided that he is a student.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amount calculated under specific sections; conditions of payment apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-month waiting period for disability pension
rubrics_metrics.description: No pension is payable before the lapse of four months following the date of the onset of the contributor's disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective date of payment normally set four months after onset as determined by Medical Branch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application initiation documents (disability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must fill in prescribed pension application form (sent to Disability Division) and arrange physician to fill medical report form (sent to Medical Branch); must enclose birth certificate(s) and a signed authorization for release of medical information; indicate usual employment and length of time pursued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimant initiates two files (administrative and medical); authorization allows Board to obtain medical records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physician's medical report content and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Physician must provide information useful to Board's medical advisers to establish whether applicant is suffering from a sickness/infirmity of indefinite duration rendering him incapable regularly of pursuing an occupation; urged to submit report quickly and to contact Medical Branch if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaflet advises physicians not to fill in report if condition is benign; report should focus on functional limitations and avoid irrelevant medical detail; attach relevant medical records as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physician's opinion on severity and duration (SAC recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: SAC proposes expressly inviting the physician to give his opinion on the severity and duration of the disability in terms of the definitions provided under section 109.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to reduce imbalance between claimant-submitted proof and Board's counter-proof; make medical reports more precise and legally framed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for filing (disability and general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: No absolute time limit is indicated for submission of benefit applications; to safeguard full benefits claimant must submit within the year following onset of the disability; Board may not fix disability date prior to the 12 months immediately preceding submission, absent timely written notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimant's notice within one-year time limit can preserve retroactivity; late submissions may be mitigated by prior written notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role division: Disability Division vs Medical Branch
rubrics_metrics.description: Disability Division verifies documents in the file (except medical data) and ensures eligibility conditions; Medical Branch evaluates the applicant's disability in light of section 109, using medical report and occupational background and may obtain additional information or order further examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical Branch works collegially with vocational counsellor; may examine hospitalization records at Board expense; further medical exams at Board cost are possible though rarely used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of functional rehabilitation (counsellor role)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of claimant's prospects of being functionally rehabilitated depends on a listing of trades and occupations; the counsellor identifies employment possibilities suited to residual capacity viewed as illustrations of possible work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employment listings are illustrative, not exhaustive; Board will specify employment possibilities only if decision is challenged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical Branch reporting style and privacy constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Medical Branch reports are often fairly vague, do not usually mention a precise diagnosis (considered a privacy issue), and do not specify employment possibilities at this stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports state conclusions about capacity (e.g., capable of light gainful work) without detailed diagnoses; claimant bears onus to prove severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision content and notification (favourable vs unfavourable)
rubrics_metrics.description: If favourable, the Disability Division notifies claimant and specifies date effective when payment begins (normally four months after onset); if unfavourable, Claims Division/Disability Division sends signed letter accompanied by copy of Medical Branch opinion, informs right to request reconsideration (within one year) and includes reconsideration form (post-1975).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unfavourable letters summarize reasons; since 1975 reconsideration application form is included, increasing requests for reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and methods of benefit control (disability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose is to ensure beneficiary has not regained capacity to regularly pursue substantially gainful occupation; Board may require periodic medical examinations by regulation and may prescribe a medical re-examination at a predetermined date if recovery likely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematic checks via income tax data and questionnaires have been used; failure to respond to questionnaires can lead to automatic suspension of pension payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of contributors' children's and orphans' pensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Board exercises control over school attendance and marital status of beneficiaries aged 18–25 and has progressively intensified verification, subjecting all recipients to verification in 1977.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stringent control has led to disqualification of hundreds of beneficiaries annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retirement pension entitlement change (age 65)
rubrics_metrics.description: An eligible contributor acquires an absolute right to the full amount of his pension, regardless of employment income, as soon as he attains age 65 (changed from age 70).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminates need for continual earnings control for retirement beneficiaries under 70; calculation rules unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required for survivor's benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Application for survivor's benefits must be accompanied by a statement of the deceased contributor's pensionable earnings (tax slips or employer attestation), proof of death, applicant's birth certificate, and the marriage certificate; where applicant is not legal spouse, Board will advise what further evidence of cohabitation, duration, and public recognition is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant's statement may suffice unless contradicted; third-party testimony and investigator inquiries/sworn statements may be used if contradictory evidence exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required for orphan's and death benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: To substantiate an application for orphan's benefits, applicant need merely submit a birth certificate; for death benefits every application must be supported by proof of the contributor's death and establish claimant's title (heir) or that he assumed the expense of last illness/interment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial orphan stage does not require proof of school attendance for 18–25-year-old; death benefits have specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for various benefit applications
rubrics_metrics.description: No general time limit except: death benefits must be submitted within five years of contributor's death (effective 1977); no application can be made retroactive to more than twelve months for other benefits; retirement pension applications may not be submitted more than six months before pension becomes due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different benefits have different statutory filing windows; retroactivity limited to 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Division file checking and processing timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims Division checks file contents (dates, authenticity); if file complete it transmits decision to Benefits Division; computerized roll updated weekly; theoretically favourable decision could operate in five working days but in practice processing takes two to four weeks depending on workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing time varies by month and volume of pending applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of contentious/reserved cases (escalation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases involving section 105 (and formerly 107) and other difficult/doubtful matters are set aside and referred to the Technical Office; Claims Division completes files via regional investigations and prepares a short report; Technical Office team of three examines file, requests further information, prepares draft decision; disagreements escalate to Claims Division head, Technical Office head, and Legal Branch as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure provides internal checks and hierarchical resolution before final decision; reasons summarized and placed on file for possible reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content of negative decision notices for insufficient contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative decisions for insufficient contributions are communicated by means of a computer-printed form which includes mention of right to ask for reconsideration, a form for addressing such a request, and information service telephone number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other unfavourable decisions use a form letter summarizing reasons and include reconsideration form; favourable decisions indicate amount, date payable, and expected first payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit control frequency and enforcement measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately one-half of beneficiaries in categories (retirement, survivor, orphans) are called annually to declare income or provide schooling evidence; failure to answer questionnaires within prescribed period can result in automatic suspension of pension payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls have led to disqualification of thousands of beneficiaries; changes in statutory age have reduced need for control for retirement pensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and composition of Reconsideration Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconsideration is brought before the Board's board of directors but delegated to its Reconsideration Committee, chaired by the President-Director General; committee has five members, two are Board officials, majority are individuals unconnected with decision-making services and not members of civil service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee is intended to provide hierarchical review and a degree of independence (majority external members); PDG is a judge which may affect the character of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and time limits for reconsideration of pensionable earnings
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions contesting the amount of pensionable earnings are prescribed in four years from the date on which earnings/contributions were entered on the Record of Earnings, although the Board may proceed after expiry on new facts or to transfer amounts between contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributor who requested a statement of earnings can resort to reconsideration to challenge a subsequent reduction of credited contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation formalities for reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The application form for reconsideration invites applicant to present in ten to fifteen lines the reasons for reconsideration and to submit documentation; notification informs him he must submit request within twelve months following initial decision; Board will generally accept mere letters of intent and will date the process from receipt of such a letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board is not excessively formalistic; Reconsideration Committee may refuse late applications constituting a preliminary jurisdiction decision not appealable to the Social Affairs Commission.
